name: Pegvisomant

lead: Pegvisomant (Somavert) is an injectable drug that blocks the growth hormone receptor. It is approved for acromegaly, a condition of GH excess causing enlarged hands, feet and facial features.
It appears in appearance discussions as a GH-axis compound. No published study tests it for cosmetic use.

paras: It binds the GH receptor and prevents GH from signaling, which lowers IGF-1.
The label lists liver enzyme elevations, hypoglycemia in diabetic patients, injection-site lipohypertrophy and hypersensitivity. It is prescription-only.

lead: Pegvisomant, sold as Somavert, is a pegylated growth hormone (GH) analog that blocks the GH receptor. [1][2] It is approved in the US for acromegaly in patients who responded inadequately to surgery or radiation, or for whom those are unsuitable, with the treatment goal of normalizing IGF-1. [2]

Acromegaly produces enlargement of the hands, feet and facial features, which is why the drug is sometimes mentioned in appearance and height forums as a GH-axis compound. No published trial in the supplied literature tests it for cosmetic purposes in people without GH excess. [3][4]
Documented risks in the label include hypoglycemia in patients with diabetes, liver toxicity, lipohypertrophy and systemic hypersensitivity. [2]

paras: The US label indication is acromegaly after inadequate response to surgery or radiation, or when those are not appropriate. [2] Grokipedia describes a pediatric use in pituitary gigantism as investigational. [1] A phase 3 study of children with growth hormone excess has been registered. [5]

A 12-week randomized double-blind study in 112 acromegaly patients tested three pegvisomant doses against placebo, and a long-term study followed 160 patients for an average of 425 days. [3][4] Grokipedia reports IGF-1 normalization in most patients over the long term. [1] The ACROSTUDY surveillance reviewed 1288 subjects for long-term safety. [6]

The label lists hypoglycemia in patients with diabetes, liver toxicity (transaminase elevations above ten times the upper limit were reported in a small share of patients), cross-reactivity with GH assays, lipohypertrophy and systemic hypersensitivity. [2] Animal studies showed fetotoxicity at a high dose and human pregnancy data are insufficient. [2]

Pegvisomant binds GH receptors and blocks endogenous GH signaling, which lowers serum IGF-1 and other GH-responsive proteins. [2] It is a 191-amino-acid recombinant protein with attached polyethylene glycol, which changes its pharmacokinetics. [1][7] Because it blocks the receptor rather than suppressing secretion, GH assays may be unreliable during treatment. [2]

Randomized and long-term studies have been performed in acromegaly. [3][4][6][8] Registered studies also cover bone microarchitecture in acromegaly, quality of life, children with GH excess, pre-diabetes and severe insulin resistance. [5][9][10][11] No studies were found of pegvisomant for cosmetic or height purposes in healthy people.
